question: In the early history of Madras, the settlement was divided into 'White Town' and 'Black Town'. Which of the following accurately describes this administrative and social division?
options: White Town consisted of the area inside Fort St. George occupied by Europeans, while Black Town was the native settlement housing Indian merchants, weavers, and artisans
White Town housed civilian English administrators, while Black Town was the cantonment for the local sepoy garrison
White Town was the British trading quarters, while Black Town was the area controlled by French and Dutch merchants within the city limits
White Town was the commercial area under the Mayor's Court, while Black Town was governed by the traditional panchayat system
explanation: The English settlement at Madras was strictly segregated. 'White Town' was the fortified area (inside Fort St. George) where Europeans resided and conducted administrative/military affairs. 'Black Town' (originally Madraspatnam and Chennapatnam) lay outside the fort walls and was populated by Indian weavers, merchants, brokers, and artisans who supplied goods to the British.
